html:
The Great Council of Chiefs was a body of Fijian chiefs set up by the British governor Arthur Gordon in 1876 to advise on Fijian affairs. It became one of the most powerful institutions in Fiji.

Under the colony it helped run the Fijian administration. After independence it chose the president and part of the senate, and it backed Fijian control of politics after the coups of 1987.

The military government of Frank Bainimarama suspended the council in 2007 and abolished it in 2012 as a barrier to equal citizenship. The government elected in 2022 brought it back in 2023.
